To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The global transcriptional regulator FIS modulates cellular topoisomerization and thus the overall DNA supercoiling; 2) FIS binds to supercoiled circular DNA molecules in vitro leading to the formation of apical loops; 3) The FIS-induced loops are stabilized by the formation of branche junctions; 4) FIS binds preferentially to the upstream regions of the stable RNA promoters, where it acts as a topologically active protein; 5
FIS, a global transcriptional regulator of metabolism, is able to control the level of DNA supercoiling and that it acts as a topoisomerase modulator and as a topological regulator of transcription.
1. The FIS protein is a global transcriptional regulator and topological homeostat, which modulates the superhelicity and topology of DNA in vivo and in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between the global and local effects exerted by architectural proteins on DNA supercoiling and its functional consequences.
the interplay between the global and local effects exerted by architectural proteins on DNA topology, and its functional implications.
the interplay between the global effect exerted on DNA topology by architectural proteins and their local effects on promoter regions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FIS acts as an architectural protein, a global transcriptional regulator and a DNA topological homeostat.
FIS is a transcriptional regulator that modulates DNA topology and, in this manner, optimises the activity of its target promoters.
FIS is a transcription factor which acts as a topoisomerase modulator and, in turn, a topological homeostasis regulator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

FIS is a global transcriptional regulator that also modulates the activity of cellular DNA topoisomerase(s) to maintain a specific DNA topology that is required for the optimal activity of some promoters.
transcription factors are not only global regulators of gene expression, but they also act as topological homeostats that optimise the energy of the DNA supercoil for gene expression.
FIS is a global topological homeostat that modulates the activity of DNA topoisomerases in order to maintain a constant superhelicity level in the cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
global and local DNA topologies are tightly coupled and that the global topology is an important determinant of gene expression.
the global effects of architectural proteins on DNA supercoiling may not be merely a consequence of their local effects on specific promoters.
the global and local effects of FIS are not mutually exclusive, rather they are intimately linked to each other.
